data.turoyo: Fəlgi d-yawmo komaʕrən daʔəm bərġəl apraxe w dawqe ḥamiʕe w košotən dawġe ste barra dəṯṯe.
data.translation: Mittags essen sie stets Weizengrütze, Blätterfüllsel, gesäuerte Fladenbrate und trinken Ayran dazu.

rationale: New Part act. box: plural attributive ḥamiʕe describes fermented/leavened flatbreads, result state of the existing sense.

summary: The JL passage contrasts Infectum gḥoməʕ during rising with Preterit Intransitive ḥaməʕ as a completed prerequisite to flattening. Both are non-agentive I forms; no Detransitive is needed.
Part act. ḥamiʕe provides an attributive result-state counterpart on dawqe. The edition’s unusual spelling Fladenbrate is retained verbatim.

The assigned JL 9.10/5 source contains inline 006, while the existing entry cites JL 9.10.6. The supplied German translates only the material before 006. Preserve existing citations until segmentation is verified; do not attach that German to either fermentation token.
Restore the edition translation after inline 006 in assigned JL 9.10/5 and verify its relation to existing JL 9.10.6; both new token quotations are withheld.
Is ḥamiʕe (94/272) a productive Part act. of ḥmʕ or a lexical adjective of sourness? The proposed box follows the form and food-fermentation context, with no separate taste sense.
Attributive ḥamiʕe names the fermented/leavened state of flatbreads; retain with säuern, aufgehen rather than infer a separate taste sense.
